baslik: Why Challenger Broke Apart 73 Seconds After Launch

sahneler.metin: Seventy-three seconds after launch, Challenger broke apart.
Seven astronauts were killed, in front of the world.
The cause was just a rubber ring, a quarter-inch thick.
Overnight, temperatures fell well below freezing.
Cold made the O-rings stiff, so they couldn't seal the booster joint.
Burning gas escaped the joint and cut into the fuel tank.
Engineers had warned against launching in the cold the night before.
They were overruled. Today, that warning is taught to every engineer.

aciklama:
On January 28, 1986, Space Shuttle Challenger broke apart 73 seconds after launch. A cold-stiffened O-ring in a solid rocket booster joint failed to seal.
